title: Domination is equivalent to universal injectivity of the pushout leg
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $a:P\to Q$, $b:P\to Q'$ be $R$-linear maps. Form their pushout $Q''=Q\amalg_P Q'$ with canonical map $b':Q'\to Q''$. Say that $b$ dominates $a$ if for every $R$-module $L$ one has $\ker(a\otimes_R\mathrm{id}_L)\subseteq\ker(b\otimes_R\mathrm{id}_L)$. Then $b$ dominates $a$ if and only if $b'$ is universally injective [lem-trf-universal-injective-finite-test], meaning that $L\otimes_R b'$ is injective for every $R$-module $L$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-module-pushout-quotient-presentation] to $a,b$. It supplies $D=Q'\oplus Q$, $\delta(x)=(b(x),-a(x))$, $E=D/\delta(P)$, the quotient $\pi$, and $j(y)=\pi(y,0)$. Its statement gives $\pi$ surjective, $\ker\pi=\operatorname{im}\delta$, and a linear isomorphism $e:E\simeq Q''$ with $ej=b'$, identifying the specified $Q'$ leg.

source.place: Tag 0AUM, lemma-domination-universally-injective, proof first paragraph: quotient of the direct sum by the image of (g,-f), expanded into its universal property and exact sequence.

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary $R$-module $L$, and write $h_L=h\otimes_R\mathrm{id}_L$. The exact presentation of Step 1 meets both hypotheses on $\pi$ in [lem-trf-quotient-pair-tensor-kernel], which gives $\ker j_L=b_L(\ker a_L)$. If $\ker a_L\subseteq\ker b_L$, every element of $\ker j_L$ is $b_L(w)=0$ for some $w\in\ker a_L$, so $j_L$ is injective. Conversely, if $j_L$ is injective and $w\in\ker a_L$, the kernel identity places $b_L(w)$ in $\ker j_L=0$; hence $w\in\ker b_L$. Thus $j_L$ is injective exactly when $\ker a_L\subseteq\ker b_L$. No flatness of $L$ or injectivity of $\delta$ is required.

source.place: Tag 0AUM, lemma-domination-universally-injective, proof: tensoring the quotient pushout and its kernel sequence; Tag 00DF, lemma-tensor-product-exact, for right exactness.

proof.text: Quantifying the kernel inclusion over every $L$ is precisely domination as defined in the item. Tensoring $e$ and its inverse gives inverse maps, by compatibility with composition and identities [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]; the identity $ej=b'$ gives $e_Lj_L=(b')_L$. Thus $j_L$ is injective exactly when $(b')_L$ is. The bilinear swap $V\otimes_RL\to L\otimes_RV$, $v\otimes l\mapsto l\otimes v$, extends uniquely by the same tensor universal property, and the reverse swap is its inverse on generators. On pure tensors these swaps intertwine $b'\otimes\mathrm{id}_L$ with $\mathrm{id}_L\otimes b'$. Hence injectivity of the former for every $L$ is exactly the universal injectivity in the item. This proves both directions.
